short: Grandson of Genghis who conquered the Song and ruled China as founder of the Yuan dynasty.
full:
When Möngke died in 1259 without an heir, Kublai broke off his campaign in the south and had himself proclaimed khagan at his own kurultai at Kaiping in the spring of 1260, while his brother Ariq Böke was elected at Karakorum. Four years of war followed; Kublai, holding the grain of northern China, starved the Mongolian capital into submission. He won the title, but the western khanates never truly accepted him, and the empire was thereafter four states rather than one.

He built a new capital at Dadu, on the site of modern Beijing, proclaimed the Yuan dynasty in 1271 in the Chinese manner, and completed the conquest of the Song in 1279 — the first time all China was ruled from outside. He governed through a Mongol and foreign elite over Chinese institutions, restored the Grand Canal, and issued paper currency. Twin invasions of Japan were wrecked by typhoons, and campaigns in Vietnam and Java failed. He died on 18 February 1294, having been described at length by Marco Polo.
